It is easily accessible from the M25, via the A12. It is a short walk from Fairlop and Barkingside stations, both on the Central Line. We have 2 rooms you can hire for meetings and functions as well as a licensed bar and restaurant. Fairlop Waters Country Park is also an approved licensed venue for weddings and civil ceremonies. The country park is managed by Vision Redbridge Culture & Leisure. For more information visit the Vision website .; ; Facilities; Outdoor Activity Centre; Sailing and canoeing are available with tuition at the Centre. They also offer a variety of outdoor pursuits with equipment hire and safety tuition.; For further information visit the Outdoor Activity Centre website .; Fairlop Rowing Club; Fairlop Rowing Club has a junior and adult section that train 3 times a week. The club accepts new members that have previous rowing experience or have completed a 'Learn to Row' course. There is a waiting list for the next junior and adult Learn to Row courses so if you are interested in adding your name to the waiting list or require further information please email Fairlop Rowing Club .; Get active at Fairlop Waters; Please see the weekly activity programme ; Owls Play Centre; An indoor play area which offers fun and adventurous activity for children up to 12 years old. The play centre is multi-tiered with dedicated playzones for babies, toddlers and juniors providing a safe and secure environment for children. The centre is also available to hire for parties! Learn more about Owls on the Vision website .; Other activities; angling; bar; bike rides ; boulder park; floodlit driving range; golf course 9 & 18 hole ; golf coaching; hall and meeting rooms for hire ; nature trail (pdf 1.3MB) ; Outdoor Activity Centre ; windsurfing & sailing lake; Hire the park; Our parks and outdoor spaces including park buildings are available to hire for large or small events. For further information on how to hire a park visit our page on hiring outdoor spaces .; Training businesses; If you would like to use the park for training businesses such as bootcamps, personal training or sports coaching you will need to apply for a permit. To view their privacy policy visit the Vision RCL website .; ; Ilford War Memorial Garden ; The Memorial was built to recognise and remember the 1,159 fallen during the First World War from Ilford. It was unveiled on the 11 November 1922 by the daughter of Queen Victoria, Princess Louise, Duchess of Argyll.; Ilford War Memorial Gardens Action Group (IWMAG) has worked with local residents, businesses, visitors and Vision Redbridge Culture and Leisure to maintain the gardens and ensure our heroes are not forgotten. ; Conservation work on the “Men Of Ilford” War Memorial was completed in May 2015 with the help of The War Memorials Trust who provided partial funding of just under £5,000. ; Come and enjoy the peace and serenity of these beautiful gardens which were created in the early 1920s from the proceeds of a public appeal to provide a fitting memorial. ; ; Memorial Hall; The grounds house the Memorial Hall, inside of which are the names of the 1,159 men of Ilford who died in the Great War. It has limited open days during the year. There is no entry fee and the Memorial Hall has good access for those with restricted mobility.; Visit; Eastern Avenue Ilford IG2 7JY; Situated close to Newbury Park tube station, just north of Ilford on the A12, this site is easily accessible by public transport. Please be aware that there is no car parking at the gardens.; Loxford Park ; Loxford Park is a large park that has a lot of mature trees and shrubs that provide a great habitat for wildlife and birds. It benefits from an old sunken garden that is popular with park users wishing to rest from walking and also popular with skaters who enjoy a small skate park in this area.; The Park has a fantastic play area featuring a huge tunnel, mounds to run up and down, boulders and planting and a nest swing that can be enjoyed together by children of all ages and abilities.; For a list of facilities available please visit the Vision Website. ; Hire the park for an event ; Training businesses; To use the park for training businesses such as bootcamps, personal training or sports coaching you will need to apply for a permit visit the Vision website . All 30 trees planted were chosen for their edible features such as fruits, nuts, leaves or bark. As well as providing a source of food, as the trees mature they will become a prominent feature in the park landscape.; The trees were all planted by volunteers including local residents and primary school children. ; You can download a copy of the Loxford Park edible tree trail by visiting the Vision website .; How to Find Us; View Loxford Park on the map ; Easily accessible from Loxford Lane, Ilford or Twyford Road entrances, Barking.; Seven Kings Park ; The park has lots of features from formal rose beds for you to enjoy and plenty of seating so you can relax while out for a long stroll. It has been given a Green Flag Award and has been voted top 10 in the country in the People's Choice Award on five occasions.; The park was originally the parkland to Valentines Mansion and Gardens. ; The multi-use games area in Valentines park includes two multi goals for basketball and football. The installation was part funded by the Football Foundation and the Council’s Olympic Legacy Fund. ; Events and Activities; If you have some spare time on your hands and would like to help keep Valentines Park maintained then why not come along to one of our workdays? Or if you prefer walking, our Walking for Health group also meets regularly at Valentines Park for more details see our events listing on the Vision website . There are also weekly activities such parkrun, Dementia Walks and Talk, Tennis Coaching for more information see our regular activities timetable. ; ; People's Choice Award ; Valentines Park has once again been voted one of the Top Ten Green Flag Award-winning parks in the UK! The People’s Choice Award top ten parks were announced in a special virtual awards ceremony hosted by Keep Britain Tidy , in celebration of the 25th anniversary of the Green Flag Award. Valentines Park was among the winners, having achieved the place for the third year running and the seventh time overall since 2012, thanks to your votes.; Find out more on the Green Flag page . ; ; Facilities; Valentines Mansion and Gardens; Valentines Mansion is a beautifully restored 300 year old country house in the grounds of Valentines Park. It has a grand staircase and elegant period rooms, including the recreated Victorian kitchen and Georgian rooms with gorgeous views over surrounding parkland. The third floor has been converted into artist' studios, which visitors can often view during open studio days where they are able to meet the artists and view their work. The mansion is often host to art exhibitions and installations.; The Grade II* listed building is also perfect for a whole host of functions, from weddings and celebrations to corporate events. Valentines Mansion and Gardens also has wide varied programme of events throughout the year including guided tours, creative workshops, special events and children's holiday activities, for more details visit the Vision website. ; Café; The park has two cafés, both with a great selection of food and beverages.
